note: Instructions for the language-model coder (P0). Examples are illustrative paraphrases written for the codebook, not corpus text.

codes.label: relevance
codes.definition: Is the segment about the Super Bowl halftime show, the headliner's selection or the rival show? Asked first, in a separate call.

levels.yes: about the halftime show, the selection, reactions to it, or the rival show
levels.no: anything else, including the performer's music, tours or awards, other people named Benito, game coverage, advertising and schedules

decision_rules: Only V0 = yes segments are coded for V1–V3.

codes.label: primary frame
codes.definition: The one frame the segment stresses most: what it selects and makes salient about the halftime show.

levels.national identity: what the nation is, its symbols and who represents it (anthem, flag, 'American' culture)
levels.immigration: migration, borders, deportation, legal status, ICE
levels.cultural representation: Latino or Puerto Rican culture, language, music and visibility on a national stage
levels.political controversy: the selection as an act of officials and institutions disputed in politics (statements by officials, boycotts, the rival show)
levels.generic partisan conflict: the event as a fight between political sides (left vs right, Democrats vs Republicans, media bias) tied to which side is right about the show
levels.no frame: a relevant segment that stresses none of the five frames

examples: Illustrative: 'The NFL picked a singer who won't even perform in English' → national identity, unless immigration is named
Illustrative: 'Democrats love him, Republicans hate him, it's the culture war again' → generic partisan conflict
decision_rules: Code the frame that takes most of the segment's text; if two tie, prefer the frame tied to the event (national identity, immigration, cultural representation) over political controversy, and political controversy over generic partisan conflict.

codes.label: belonging line
codes.definition: Whether the segment draws a line around the nation that places the performer or his audience inside it (include) or outside it (exclude).

levels.include: the performer, Puerto Ricans, Latinos or Spanish speakers are treated as legitimately American
levels.exclude: they are treated as not, or not fully, American, or as not fit to represent the country

examples: Illustrative: 'He is as American as anyone; Puerto Rico is the United States' → include
Illustrative: 'Get someone who represents America' → exclude
decision_rules: Code the line the segment's speakers draw, not the coder's view.
A line reported and rejected by the anchor is coded by what the anchor asserts.
Mixed lines: code the line that takes most of the segment.

A line counts only when it is drawn around the nation: who is or is not American. Talk that places a politician, a party or its voters on one side of a dispute is not a belonging line, even when it uses the words of membership (e.g. 'real Americans vote for us' about voters is partisan; 'he is not American' about the performer is exclude).

codes.label: evaluation of Spanish
codes.definition: For segments that name the Spanish language or singing in Spanish: how the use of Spanish is judged.

levels.claim to belonging: Spanish is treated as part of America or as a legitimate claim to be included
levels.breach of belonging: Spanish is treated as foreign, divisive or improper for a national stage
levels.neither: Spanish is named without an evaluation
levels.not named: the segment does not name the language

examples: Illustrative: 'Half the country speaks Spanish at home' → claim to belonging
Illustrative: 'Nobody will understand a word of it' → breach of belonging
decision_rules: Code only explicit mentions of the language; music or accent alone is not named.

codes.label: derived segment types
codes.definition: Rule-coded from C1 and C2 for on-topic segments (V1 ≠ none): a belonging frame (V4) has V2 = include or exclude; a generic partisan conflict frame (V5) has V1 = political controversy or generic partisan conflict and V2 = none.
decision_rules: Computed by script after P0; never coded by the model.

codes.label: network and phase
codes.definition: Rule-coded from Archive metadata: network by channel (MSNBC and MS NOW one outlet, A9); phase by airing date against the A5 boundaries (Eastern Time).
decision_rules: An airing that crosses midnight takes the date of its start.

codes.label: analytic category
codes.definition: Rule-coded for relevant segments: belonging-include (V2 include); belonging-exclude (V2 exclude); otherwise the V1 frame (national identity, immigration, cultural representation, political controversy, generic partisan conflict, no frame).
decision_rules: Computed by script after P0; never coded by the model.

dictionaries.note: Word lists for the rule-based checks (A25) and the topic-model fit rule (A24); fixed before collection; matched case-insensitively on whole words and phrases; the filter keywords and generic words ('American', 'language') are excluded; agreement with the model code reported as Krippendorff's alpha.

human_checkers: Two of the authors code V0–V3 for the spot-check sample from this codebook alone, after a practice round on segments outside the sample; they never see the model's codes (A35).
